Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

agetime 1.0.0

  • Initial CRAN release.

  • New functions age_set_order_tree(), period_set_order_tree(), and cohort_set_order_tree() order the levels of labels that form a reporting tree, such as census tables with detailed ages, broad ages, and age not stated. Levels are ordered as leaves (by lower limit), then broader groups (each after the groups inside it), then missing values. Leaves can lie at different depths. Overlapping labels that do not nest, and totals, are errors.

  • The diagnose and assert functions for ages, periods, and cohorts (for instance age_diagnose_values() and age_assert_levels()) have a new condition, valid_tree, which checks that labels form a reporting tree: labels nest, and the most detailed labels cover the full span with no gaps, so that every broader label is divided exactly into narrower ones.

  • The assert functions (for instance age_assert_values() and cohort_assert_levels()) have new arguments x_arg and call, for use inside other functions. Error messages now name the labels being checked, as in “Age group labels in age fail check no_gap”. By default, errors name the assert function; a calling function can supply call = rlang::current_env() so that errors, including errors from parsing labels, name that function instead. agetime now imports rlang (previously an indirect dependency).

  • All functions that take labels (for instance age_lower(), age_coarsen_to(), age_fill(), and period_set_open_left()) now have arguments x_arg and call, like the assert functions, so that they can be used inside other functions. x_arg names the labels in error and warning messages, and defaults to the expression supplied for labels. call gives the function to name in messages: by default the agetime function itself, but a calling function can supply call = rlang::current_env(). Functions with a second set of labels have a second name argument: to_arg for the coarsen_to() functions, and y_arg for the mapping() functions. The diagnose functions have x_arg only. Functions that create labels (for instance age_labels()) are unchanged.

  • Messages about labels that cannot be interpreted now name the labels, as in “Can’t interpret labels in age”, followed by the details. Messages from the coarsen functions name the labels being coarsened, as in “Can’t coarsen age groups in age”.

  • New functions age_labels_tree(), period_labels_tree(), and cohort_labels_tree() create labels for a reporting tree: detailed labels from breaks, broader labels given through nodes (nesting to any depth), and "Missing" for not stated (included by default). Labels are returned in the same order as *_set_order_tree().

Developed by John Bryant, Junni Zhang.
